pages.title: How It Works
pages.content:
How it works

How It Works

Yukisaki Route simplifies morning courier dispatch into four predictable steps from address import to the printed round sheet. Here is how your depot moves from evening files to departure before the vans leave.

Four steps

From evening file to printed sheet

Import

The evening before, or at 05:30

The dispatcher imports tomorrow's delivery addresses the evening before or at 05:30. Yukisaki Route takes the raw stop list and organizes every stop into clean road order for fleets running 3 to 25 vans.

See the round sheet

Road order

3 to 25 vans, 40 to 600 stops a day

Instead of sorting paperwork by hand or guessing street sequences in the dark, your desk sees a clear delivery sequence built around sensible driving corridors. Fleets handling 40 to 600 stops a day get balanced routes generated without delay. The software prepares each round so the team can review the workload before drivers arrive at the depot yard.

See the prices

Print

One sheet per driver

Once the stop sequence is approved, the desk prints one clean round sheet for each driver. The printed sheet lists every stop in road sequence with time windows, parcel counts, and specific desk notes clearly visible. Drivers take their sheet directly into the cab, keeping their day organized without navigating complex menus or draining phone batteries. For drivers who prefer a screen, the identical round order updates simultaneously in the mobile phone view. Vans leave the yard on time, loaded according to the sheet.

Read the questions
Start the 14-day trial

The dispatcher

The dispatcher has the last word

Software can sequence roads, but your dispatcher knows the local ground. Gate codes, quiet back alleys, pedestrian morning hours, and shops that open late are details that belong to experienced depot staff.

Paper-first dispatch※1

Yukisaki Route leaves full control at the desk.
The dispatcher reviews the suggested stop sequence on screen and adjusts any van run with a single click.
The software never overrides the human dispatcher.

Start the 14-day trial

※1 The sheet always shows the desk’s last edit.

pages.title: The Round Sheet
pages.content:
The round sheet

The Round Sheet

The round sheet is the physical centre of Yukisaki Route, giving each driver a single clear page in exact road order. It removes cab confusion and keeps morning loading calm.

The page in the cab

What is on the sheet

Round sheet

One page per driver, in road order

Every printed round sheet presents four core details arranged for quick reading in low cab light.

  • Stop orderThe strict stop order, guiding the driver from the depot gates through every drop in sequence.
  • Time windowThe delivery time window, showing committed morning slots and business opening hours.
  • Parcel countThe exact parcel count for each stop, allowing drivers to organize their cargo hold during morning loading.
  • Desk noteThe desk note, highlighting specific instructions like gate codes or rear entrance access.
See how it works
Start the 14-day trial

Paper-first dispatch※1

Paper-first dispatch in the depot yard

Physical paper remains the most reliable dispatch tool in a working yard. A printed sheet does not break when dropped on wet asphalt, requires no battery charging, and works through winter rain and thick work gloves. Drivers can clip the page to the sun visor or dashboard and mark completed stops with a pen as they step back into the cab. It creates an immediate, tangible record that stays with the van throughout the entire morning round without software distraction.

※1 Paper and phone show the same sequence.

On the phone

The live mobile phone view

Alongside the printed paper, Yukisaki Route mirrors the exact same round order to the driver's phone.

Same order, on the phone

If a customer calls the depot to reschedule or an urgent morning parcel is added before departure, the phone view updates the sequence instantly.
Drivers can tap an address to open navigation or read gate codes directly from their mobile screen when walking up to an apartment entrance.
Paper and mobile work together, sharing one consistent sequence from the morning desk.

Start the 14-day trial

pages.title: 14-Day Free Trial
pages.content:
Trial

14-Day Free Trial

Test Yukisaki Route with your own depot address files for 14 days without entering credit card details. See how your morning rounds run when planned in road order before departure.

Start

Start your depot trial

Starting your trial requires four simple fields: your name, courier firm, number of vans between 3 and 25, and your email address. We do not ask for credit card numbers or payment details to begin. Within minutes, your account is ready to receive your daily delivery spreadsheets or address lists. Fleets handling between 40 and 600 stops a day can run their complete fleet on the trial, with support available Monday to Saturday from 05:30 to 14:00 CET.

No card needed. The trial ends by itself on day 14.

The fourteen days

The fourteen-day test schedule

Day 1

Import and print

On Day 1, import your addresses and print your first test round sheet to examine the road order.

Days 2–3

Run it beside your usual plan

During Days 2 and 3, run the printed sheets alongside your usual delivery routine to compare driving flow.

Days 4–7

Sheets alone at the yard

Across Days 4 to 7, rely on the sheets alone at the depot yard during morning departures.

Days 8–14

Decide

From Days 8 to 14, evaluate the depot results and decide if the software fits your daily operation.

After the trial

What happens after day 14

Your trial ends automatically after fourteen days. Because no payment details are collected at registration, nothing is ever charged to your account when the period concludes.

Nothing is charged※1

If you choose not to subscribe to a monthly plan, the trial ends automatically on day 14 and access simply pauses.
You can export all your route data, stop histories, and address files upon request at any point.
If you wish to continue, your saved depot settings and rounds carry over seamlessly.

pages.title: Customer Stories
pages.content:
Stories

Customer Stories

Read how four independent courier firms organize their daily delivery rounds across European towns and rural districts. These regional fleets rely on printed round sheets every morning.

Four firms

How their mornings run now

Kade Couriers

Ghent · 6 vans · 210 stops · Retail deliveries across Ghent

Operating from Ghent, Kade Couriers runs 6 vans handling 210 stops every day, delivering shop parcels to retail businesses and downtown boutiques. Before switching to Yukisaki Route, their morning loading was delayed by drivers trying to coordinate pedestrian-zone delivery windows and narrow canal lanes. Today, the dispatcher imports shop orders the evening before. When drivers arrive at the depot at dawn, each van receives a printed round sheet arranged in exact street sequence. Morning deliveries finish smoothly before afternoon retail traffic builds up in the city centre.

Valmara Express

Porto · 11 vans · 380 stops · Scheduled pharmacy runs in Porto

Valmara Express operates 11 vans handling 380 stops across Porto, specializing in scheduled morning deliveries to local pharmacies, clinics, and care homes. Medical supplies require precise arrival windows and reliable chain-of-custody handovers. Their dispatcher uses Yukisaki Route to lock in priority hospital drop-offs first, allowing the remaining urban route to assemble in natural road order. Drivers carry their printed round sheet into each pharmacy counter, recording signatures and noting gate codes directly on paper while checking urgent updates on their mobile screens.

Norrby Bud

Malmö · 4 vans · 90 stops · Morning florists and bakeries in Malmö

In Malmö, Norrby Bud operates 4 vans completing 90 stops each morning, delivering fresh goods to neighbourhood bakeries and florists before 09:00. Early delivery requires drivers to navigate locked service courtyards, narrow back doors, and silent residential streets before sunrise. With Yukisaki Route, gate codes and specific access notes are printed directly beside each shop address on the driver's morning sheet. The team loads crates in reverse drop sequence and leaves the yard without delays, completing every drop well before morning shop doors open.

Lindenhof Kurier

Freiburg · 14 vans · 460 stops · Mixed town and rural rounds in Freiburg

Lindenhof Kurier manages 14 vans and 460 stops from their yard in Freiburg, serving both dense historic quarters and outlying Black Forest valleys. Drivers often encounter dead mobile signals and winding mountain roads where digital navigation fails. Having a physical round sheet on the dashboard gives drivers uninterrupted route guidance regardless of cellular coverage. The dispatcher adjusts routes for known roadwork and steep country lanes before printing, ensuring both town vans and rural runs leave the depot fully prepared for the day ahead.

pages.title: About Yukisaki Route
pages.content:
About

About Yukisaki Route

Yukisaki Route was built in 2019 to give regional courier dispatchers calm, practical software for morning route organization. We believe small delivery fleets deserve dependable tools built around how yards actually work.

Since 2019

Why we built Yukisaki Route in 2019

Yukisaki Route BV was founded in 2019 at Noorderhaven 18, 9000 Ghent, Belgium. We started the company after watching small courier depots struggle every morning with generic route software designed for corporate long-haul logistics. Regional fleets running 3 to 25 vans do not need complex tracking algorithms or intrusive cab monitors. They need clean road order, dependable address imports, and paper round sheets that drivers can hold in their hands during dawn yard loading.

Founders

Two people, one desk

Ines Vermeulen

Co-founder · eight years on a courier desk

Ines Vermeulen is co-founder and spent eight years managing a busy courier desk, experiencing firsthand the stress of morning dispatch deadlines and missing gate codes. She leads product design to keep the software practical for working dispatchers.

Tomasz Zielinski

Co-founder · engineering

Tomasz Zielinski is co-founder and oversees engineering, focusing on dependable database architecture and fast address sequencing. Together, they designed Yukisaki Route to solve real morning depot problems without adding unnecessary complexity to the dispatch desk.

pages.title: Frequently Asked Questions
pages.content:
FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Find clear answers to common questions about our 14-day trial, dispatch software features, and monthly billing. Our team is available every morning to assist your depot desk.

Trial

How does the 14-day free trial work?

The 14-day trial gives your courier firm complete access to Yukisaki Route without entering credit card details or signing a contract. You can configure up to 25 vans and import your daily address lists starting on day one. Your dispatcher can generate road-order sequences, print physical driver round sheets, and view routes on mobile devices. Support is available throughout the trial from Monday to Saturday, between 05:30 and 14:00 CET, ensuring your morning desk gets immediate assistance.

Do I need a credit card to start the trial?

No credit card is required to begin your trial. We believe courier managers should test the software in their actual depot yard before making any financial commitment. You simply enter your name, company name, van fleet size between 3 and 25 vehicles, and your email address. Because payment details are never taken upfront, you will never experience surprise charges, automatic roll-overs, or unexpected billing when your fourteen trial days conclude.

What fleet size is the trial designed for?

The trial is built specifically for regional courier fleets operating between 3 and 25 vans handling 40 to 600 stops each day. This focus ensures our routing tools match regional yard operations where dispatchers know their drivers by name. The trial includes all features for your entire fleet up to 25 vans, allowing you to run your whole operation on the software rather than testing a restricted single-vehicle demo.

How should our depot test the software during the first week?

We suggest testing the software across four stages. On Day 1, import your stops and print a test round sheet to examine the road order. During Days 2 and 3, run the printed sheets alongside your existing routing routine to compare driving flow. Across Days 4 to 7, rely entirely on the printed round sheets in the yard. Finally, during Days 8 to 14, evaluate depot feedback and decide whether to subscribe.

What happens when our 14-day trial ends?

When your fourteen days end, your account access simply pauses. Nothing is charged automatically because no billing details were collected. If you decide Yukisaki Route is not right for your depot, you do not need to call to cancel. If you need your route records or stop histories, our team will provide a complete data export upon request. If you choose to subscribe, all your settings carry over.

Software

How does the dispatcher import daily delivery addresses?

Dispatchers can import addresses the evening before delivery or early in the morning at 05:30. You upload your daily stop list using standard spreadsheet files or CSV exports from your order system. Priya Raman on our data team ensures file formats import smoothly. Once uploaded, the software verifies addresses, groups them by vehicle, and arranges every drop into clean road order, ready for the dispatcher to review and adjust.

Can the dispatcher adjust routes before printing?

Yes. We believe the human dispatcher always has the final word on delivery sequences. While our software calculates logical road order, local staff understand temporary road closures, morning school traffic, quiet alleys, and specific customer delivery hours. The dispatcher can reorder stops, shift parcels between vans, or add special instructions with a single click. The printed round sheet reflects the dispatcher's exact adjustments, never an unchangeable automated calculation.

What information appears on the printed round sheet?

The printed round sheet provides four essential details for the driver: the sequential stop order, the assigned delivery time window, the exact parcel count for each stop, and specific desk notes. Desk notes include gate access codes, rear loading door directions, or customer opening hours. Everything is printed clearly on a single page, allowing the driver to organize their van hold and check off completed deliveries with a pen.

Is there a mobile view for drivers on the road?

Yes, the round sheet is mirrored on the driver's mobile phone view. While we encourage paper-first dispatch for cab organization and reliable offline access, drivers can view the exact same stop sequence on their phone. Tapping an address opens navigation, and drivers can view updated gate codes or note changes while walking to a delivery door. The mobile view stays synchronized with any midday updates entered at the depot desk.

Does the software suit long-haul trucking or instant on-demand couriers?

No. Yukisaki Route is specifically designed for small regional courier firms running scheduled multi-drop rounds. We do not support long-haul interstate trucking or instant on-demand motorbike dispatch where parcels are booked and assigned dynamically every few minutes. Our platform focuses entirely on depot operations running 3 to 25 vans with 40 to 600 daily stops, where tomorrow's delivery addresses are prepared either the evening before or early in the morning.

Billing

How much does Yukisaki Route cost after the trial?

Subscription pricing depends on the size of your fleet. For smaller depots running 3 to 5 vans, the Yard plan costs €24 per van / month. For larger operations running 6 to 25 vans, the Depot plan costs €19 per van / month. Couriers with multiple locations can add an Extra depot for €40 per depot / month. All subscription prices are quoted in EUR, excl. VAT, billed on a regular monthly basis.

What is the optional guided set-up morning?

The Guided set-up morning is an optional onboarding service priced at €180 once. Amara Nwosu or another member of our implementation team works directly with your dispatcher over phone and screen share during a working morning dispatch. We assist with initial address import formatting, verify depot parameter settings, and help print your first live round sheets. It provides reassurance for teams wanting dedicated guidance during their initial switch.

Are prices shown with VAT?

No. All prices are in EUR, excl. VAT, billed monthly.

What support is included with our subscription?

Every subscription includes direct access to our early support team from Monday to Saturday, between 05:30 and 14:00 CET. Because courier depots start operations long before standard business hours, Sofía Morales and our support desk are online when your morning dispatch takes place. Whether you encounter an unexpected address import format or need assistance adjusting a round sheet before vans leave, our team is available to assist your desk immediately.

Waitlist

Cargo-Bike Waitlist

We are developing dedicated round sequencing tools for urban cargo-bike courier fleets operating in historic city centres. Sign up for early access notifications as development progresses.

Coming

Cargo-bike rounds are coming

Urban logistics are evolving rapidly across European cities, with pedal-assist cargo bikes handling an increasing share of downtown parcel deliveries. Cargo bikes face different routing constraints than standard vans, including pedestrian precinct regulations, bridge stairs, dedicated cycle paths, bollards, and low cargo volume limits. We are building specialized route planning features tailored to urban cargo-bike rounds, applying our proven paper-first dispatch philosophy to pedal-powered delivery fleets.

Early access

Join the early access list

Courier firms operating cargo bikes in urban centres can register for early access by submitting their name, email address, and city. As Kenji Arai and our engineering team adapt our road-order algorithms for cycle infrastructure, waitlist participants will receive early testing invitations and preview releases. We will share development milestones directly with registered couriers, ensuring new cycle routing tools reflect the practical daily realities of bicycle dispatch.

Cargo bikes

Designed for city centre couriers

The cargo-bike edition of Yukisaki Route will retain our signature simplicity: straightforward address imports, sensible street ordering, and clear printed round sheets clipped to handlebar clipboards. Couriers will be able to balance cargo weight, respect city access hours, and navigate pedestrian shopping districts without distraction. If your company operates cargo bikes alongside vans or runs a dedicated cycle courier depot, join our waitlist to help shape our cycle dispatch tools.

posts.title: Why We Still Print
posts.excerpt: In an industry chasing digital screens, the simple printed round sheet remains the calmest, most reliable tool on the depot loading dock.
posts.content:
At five in the morning, a courier yard is not an office. The concrete is cold, the overhead lights hum against the dusk, and diesel exhaust drifts across the lane as vans back into their bays. Drivers arrive with cold fingers and thermal mugs, checking the weather and preparing their vehicles for the morning run. In this environment, software that requires endless screen tapping, password logins, and constant cellular connectivity does not solve problems. It adds friction to a tight morning schedule that cannot afford delays.

When Ines Vermeulen and Tomasz Zielinski founded Yukisaki Route in 2019 at Noorderhaven 18 in Ghent, the goal was not to eliminate screens entirely, but to put them in their proper place. The dispatch computer belongs on the desk, where a dispatcher can import spreadsheet addresses, review stops in road order, and check customer notes before dawn. But once that sequence is approved, the most effective interface to hand a driver stepping into the cab is a single printed round sheet.

A printed round sheet possesses practical qualities that touchscreens cannot replicate in a working depot. Paper does not reflect morning glare across a curved windscreen. It never runs out of battery halfway through an eight-hour route in freezing rain. It does not shatter when dropped onto wet asphalt while loading heavy cardboard cartons, and it does not require a driver to remove thick work gloves to scroll through a sub-menu. Clipped to the sun visor or resting on the passenger seat, the sheet displays the entire morning sequence at a single glance.

There is also a shared clarity that comes with physical paper. In yards like Kade Couriers in Ghent or Norrby Bud in Malmö, the printed sheet is an object of common understanding between the dispatcher and the driver. Before the van doors shut, two colleagues can stand at the tailgate with a pen, reviewing an unusual gate code, noting a shop that opens late, or adjusting a priority delivery. A pen mark on paper is immediate, unmistakable, and permanent.

This does not mean mobile devices have no place in regional delivery. Yukisaki Route provides an identical, synchronized phone view for every driver on the road. If a delivery window shifts or an urgent note is added from the depot desk, the driver can view the updated stop on their screen. But the digital view serves as a quiet companion to the printed sheet, not an intrusive replacement. The driver is not forced into a rigid digital workflow that demands continuous tapping at every gate.

Small courier fleets running 3 to 25 vans succeed because their staff know their streets, their customers, and their vehicles. They do not need complex enterprise tracking systems or automated surveillance. They need a dependable road order laid out before the vans leave, and a clear sheet of paper to guide the day. In depot dispatch, simplicity is not an absence of technology; it is knowing when technology should step back and let working people do their jobs.
